conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you're here because of pain at your G-tube site. Can you tell me more about it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the pain has been getting worse. I ran out of my oxycodone a few days ago, and Tylenol just isn’t helping at all.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You’ve had this tube for a while due to your gastric bypass and hypoglycemia, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and I’ve had this pain before. I’ve been admitted a few times already. The last CT showed inflammation, but no infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Right, and your tube was exchanged, but that didn’t help much?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, it didn’t. I tried naproxen for a bit because it helped, but then I was told NSAIDs could cause ulcers, so I stopped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s correct. Given your history of ulcers, we avoid NSAIDs. We’ll start you on oxycodone again to manage the pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I just need something that works. The pain is constant and sharp.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you 10 mg every four hours as needed. We’ll also monitor for any signs of infection or complications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is there any sign of infection now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, your site looks clean—no redness or swelling. Your labs are stable too. No fever, and your white count is normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve been keeping up with my tube feeds, but they do irritate the site a little.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you on NutriHep at 50 cc/hr for now. Staying nourished is important, especially with your hypoglycemia.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been checking my blood sugar at home. It’s been okay as long as I keep feeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll continue monitoring your intake and output. You’re passing gas and having bowel movements?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve been going regularly. No nausea or vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s reassuring. We’ll encourage you to walk around a bit to keep your lungs and circulation healthy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been up a little. I feel okay, just the pain is really distracting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll reassess your pain in an hour. Let the nurse know if it’s not improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How’s the pain now after the first dose?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. Still there, but not as intense. I can actually relax a little.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. We’ll keep you on this schedule. No need for IV pain meds since the oral dose is working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I’d rather avoid IV if possible.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Vital signs are stable—no fever, heart rate and blood pressure are fine. Pain still manageable?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, as long as I take the oxycodone on time. I’ve had a few doses overnight and slept okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep monitoring. You have a few specialist appointments coming up, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I have a second opinion with a bariatric surgeon, then with Dr. Chen, and then at the Pancreas and Liver Institute to talk about pancreatectomy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Right. Those might help figure out a long-term solution. This pain seems to be chronic inflammation without infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I just want it to stop. I can’t keep coming back every time I run out of pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’re not just treating the symptom—we’re working toward a plan. For now, we’ll keep you comfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning to discharge you today. You’ve been stable, pain is controlled with oral meds, and no complications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Will I get a refill on the oxycodone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re prescribing 60 tablets, one every four hours as needed. But please don’t exceed that without talking to your doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t. What about my tube feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Resume NutriHep at 45 cc/hour. Monitor your blood sugar closely, especially if you’re not eating by mouth.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my other meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all your regular medications—fluoxetine, lansoprazole, sucralfate, rifaximin—continue as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if the pain gets worse again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your surgeon or return to the ER if pain doesn’t improve within a few hours, or if you develop fever, vomiting, or signs of dehydration.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll watch for that. And I have my follow-up appointments scheduled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Rest, stay hydrated, and keep moving around at home. Avoid driving while on pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll have someone help me at home. Thank you for getting the pain under control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll make sure your records are sent to your specialists. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before you leave. Any new symptoms?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, pain is mild now. I’ve been walking and drinking fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Discharge papers are ready. Follow up with your surgeon as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take it easy. We’re here if you need us.
